[MUQATIL:26:16-18/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Pharaoh recognized Moses, who had been raised in his house; Moses had fled Egypt after killing a person, and had lived with Pharaoh for thirty years.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some maṣdars are fixed in one syntactic position and do not inflect like ordinary verbal nouns, including not taking the article or ordinary nominative and genitive uses.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | سبحان lacks tanwīn because it became definite in usage; its accusative is like الحمد لله.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · أبو الخطاب | reports | Abu al-Khattab interprets سلاما said to a person as تسلما منك, meaning disavowal or separation.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · أبو ربيعة | reports | Abu Rabiʿa reportedly instructed people to tell someone سلاما; Abu al-Khattab explained it as disavowal.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · أمية بن أبي الصلت | reports | Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's verse uses سلامك to mean God's acquittal from every evil.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | These fixed accusatives behave like hamdan and shukran, but ordinary sources inflect whereas these expressions do not.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | غفران has سبحان's fixed-source form but not its meaning; غفرانك لا كفرانك means seeking forgiveness, not disbelief.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعض العرب | reports | Some Arabs use raised سلام when they mean mutual separation, as in سلام بسلام; the wording still substitutes for an omitted verbal expression.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Expressions such as سبحان الله and ريحانه replace full verbal phrases with an omitted verb; ريحان here means provision.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · أمية بن أبي الصلت | reports | Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's poetry attests to tanwīn on سبحان; Sībawayh compares it with the source expressions حجرا and سلاما.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | سبوحا قدوسا differs from سبحان: these are names, used with an implied أذكر when the thought or mention comes to mind.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r22] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The implied verb is omitted as in expressions replacing سبحت; the construction follows the person who remembers or recites, like أهل ذاك and صادقا.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r23] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعض العرب | reports | Some Arabs also raise سبوح قدوس, just as they raise أهل ذاك and صادق والله; Sībawayh accepts both raised and accusative usage.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r24] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The expression خير ما رد في أهل ومال is patterned like خير مقدم.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r25] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Exclamatory source accusatives such as كرما وصلفا omit a verb and substitute for أكرم به and أصلف به.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r26] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · أبو مرهب | reports | Abu Murhab's كرما وطول أنف illustrates the exclamatory source construction, equivalent to أكرم بك وأطول بأنفك.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | معاذ الله means عياذا بالله, construed as the accusative object of an unexpressed أعوذ بالله.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Sībawayh analyzes عمرك الله and قعدك الله as accusative source expressions standing for an implied verb, by analogy with نشدتك الله.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalil says the proposed verbal form عمرتك الله is an explanatory analogy, not a claim that speakers actually use it.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | An unnamed poet's عمرتك الله line attests to the expression's accusative construction.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · ابن أحمر | reports | Ibn Ahmar's verse also attests to عمرتك الله, supporting Sībawayh's analogy for عمرك الله.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · أبو الخطاب | reports | Abu al-Khattab explains سبحان الله as declaring God free of evil, like saying براءة الله من السوء.
[SIBAWAYH:ولكنهامصادروضعتموضعاواحدالاتتصرففىالكلامتصرفماذكرنامن#131/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الأعشى | reports | Al-Aʿsha's line سبحان من علقمة الفاخر supports the reported sense of disavowal from a person.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p498/r1] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī glosses walīdan as a servant and then as a young child.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p498/r2] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when Moses entered Pharaoh recognized him and reproached him: you abandoned the prophethood you now claim.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p498/r3] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · ابن عباس | reports | In another account from Ibn ʿAbbās, Pharaoh asks Moses who he is; Moses names himself as Moses son of ʿImrān, and Pharaoh then invokes having raised him as a child.
[ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p73#7/r1] ABDURRAZZAQ, d. 211 · قتادة | reports | Qatadah says Pharaoh’s family found Moses as an infant and raised him until he became a man.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p297/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | لعمرك and ولعمر الله mean “by your life” and “by God’s life”; they are oaths sworn by life.
[TAB-FULL:v1p103/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The poem says God granted the addressee a rank of honor beyond the stations attained by kings.
[TAB-FULL:v1p103/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | For those who hamza surah, it means a portion left over from the rest of the Qur’an, by analogy with a remainder of drink; al-Aʿshā’s lines use the verb for lingering residue.
[TAB-FULL:v1p103/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | An āyah can mean a sign marking where one passage ends and the next begins; the cited poem and 5:114 use it as a sign from God answering prayer. | mentions 5:114
[TAB-FULL:v1p103/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Āyah can also mean a story or message: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr calls his report an āyah, so Qur’anic āyāt can be stories following one another.
[ZAJJAJ:v4p85/r3] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | وليدا means a newborn at the time of birth.
[ZAJJAJ:v4p85/r4] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · سيبويه والخليل وجميع البصريين | reports | The lifespan word عمر has three vocalizations in ordinary use; in an oath only the open-vowel form لعمر الله is allowed, according to Sibawayh, al-Khalil, and the Basrans.
[ZAJJAJ:v4p85/r5] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Pharaoh reproaches Moses for having been raised in his household from birth until he grew up.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p470/r12] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · كلهم | reports | All readers pronounce من عمرك with the heavy form.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p470/r13] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · أبو عمرو (روايات عبيد وهرون والخفاف) | reports | Ubayd and al-Khaffaf report Abu Amr with the light form.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p470/r14] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · أبو عمرو (رواية هرون) | reports | Harun says Abu Amr did not object to the heavy alternative.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p470/r15] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · أبو عمرو (رواية عبيد بن عقيل) | reports | Ubayd ibn Aqil reports Abu Amr with the heavy form.
[IBNABIHATIM:v8p2753/r2] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · قتادة | reports | Qatāda says Pharaoh's household picked Moses up and raised him as a child until he became a man.
[NAHHAS:v3p175/r10] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | سنين is a regular sound masculine plural, though it can also be inflected on its final ن as سنينا.
[NAHHAS:v3p175/r8] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | وليدا is circumstantial; thā may assimilate into tā in ولبثت, and the heavy ḍamma of عُمْرِكَ may be dropped.
[NAHHAS:v3p175/r9] NAHHAS, d. 338 · سيبويه | reports | Sibawayh attests fatḥa on the first consonant and a silent middle consonant in عَمْر, as in the oath form لعمرك, which he says uses fatḥa for ease.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v5p356/r1] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · الجميع | reports | All canonical readers pronounce ʿumurika with a doubled mīm.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v5p356/r2] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · عبيد عن هارون والخفاف عن أبي عمرو وعبيد عن أبي عمرو | reports | These transmitters report the light form ʿumrika from Abū ʿAmr; Hārūn says Abū ʿAmr also accepted the doubled form.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v5p356/r3] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · ابن مقبل | reports | Ibn Muqbil’s line attests the form ʿumrī.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v5p356/r4] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · أبو زيد | reports | Abū Zayd cites ʿumran as another attested form.
[SULAMI:v2p72#4/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · محمد بن علي | reports | It is not chivalry to recall one's favors and lord them over a beneficiary; Pharaoh showed this lack of chivalry by reminding Moses of his upbringing.
[SULAMI:v2p72#4/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · ابن عطاء | reports | Upbringing creates a claim of care and respect; if even an enemy's raising of Moses created such a right, God's true nurturing of His servants deserves it all the more. | mentions 26:26
[THALABI:v7p160/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Pharaoh recognized Moses, who had grown up in his house, and said he had raised him as a child for thirty years before Moses killed the Copt.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v1p27/r1] MAWARDI

-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | The Arabic word for a Quranic surah has two forms: with hamza and without it.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v1p27/r10] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Abu Hurayra reports from the Prophet that the Quran came down in seven ahruf, disputing over it is disbelief (repeated three times), people should act on what they know and return what they do not know to its learned authority; no grading is stated.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v1p27/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | Without hamza, surah denotes an elevated station; the city wall is similarly named for rising above what it encloses, and al-Nabigha's verse illustrates the lofty rank meant.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v1p27/r3] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | With hamza, surah means a remaining piece, by analogy with suʾr, what remains after something is taken or drunk; al-Aʿsha's poem applies this to love left in the heart.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v1p27/r4] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet instructed drinkers to leave a remainder in the vessel, illustrating the hamzated sense of surah as what remains; no grading is stated.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v1p27/r5] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · الأعشى | reports | Al-Aʿsha's poem depicts a woman leaving a widespread crack of love in the speaker's heart when she departs, as an example of something left behind.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v1p27/r6] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | prefers | Of the two derivations of surah, the derivation without hamza is more correct.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v1p27/r7] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | One explanation of ayah is a sign marking the completion of what precedes; the verse about the heavenly table calls it a sign from God, and a line by ʿAbd Banu al-Has has uses the word similarly.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v1p27/r8] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | The Quran's use of ayah as a sign is illustrated by the disciples' request for a heavenly table as a sign from God. | mentions 5:114
[MAWARDI-FULL:v1p27/r9] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | A second explanation takes ayah to mean a story or message; Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr's poem uses it for a message, with the sense of a narrative following another narrative in sections.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | Pharaoh calls Moses a child because Moses had been a foundling in his house.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r3] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | The commentary says Moses was kept from entering for a year, left at ten, returned to call Pharaoh at thirty, and lived fifty years after Pharaoh drowned; Pharaoh cites this as a favor.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p32#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The narrative omits that Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and delivered the message before Pharaoh's reply.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p32#2/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · مقاتل | reports | Maqatil says Pharaoh recognized Moses because he had raised him in his own house.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p32#2/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Walīd here means a young child or newborn; Moses was born among them and remained there until adulthood.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p32#2/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas glosses walīd as a small child and says Moses stayed with them for eighteen years.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p32#2/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas estimates Moses' years among them at eighteen.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p32#2/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · مقاتل | reports | Maqatil estimates Moses' years among them at thirty.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p32#2/r7] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الكلبي | reports | Al-Kalbi estimates Moses' years among them at forty.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:18-20/r1] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Pharaoh says he raised Moses as a child among his people and that Moses lived there for thirty years.
[DAMGHANI:v1p365/r13] DAMGHANI, d. 478 · author | holds | Fī can mean 'with' or 'among'; Moses lived with Pharaoh's people, and Shuʿayb and Ṣāliḥ were regarded among their own peoples. | mentions 11:91, 11:62
[JISHUMI:v7p5342/r13] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Tarbiya is bringing something up through successive stages; the verb is analogous to the verb for growing.
[JISHUMI:v7p5342/r14] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | ʿUmar and ʿumr with a silent or inflected mīm are two language forms; in an oath the ʿayn is open and the mīm silent.
[JISHUMI:v7p5342/r15] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | An unnamed poet's line contrasts life with ʿumr, illustrating the word's usage.
[JISHUMI:v7p5344/r15] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Pharaoh recognized Moses and asked whether he was the child they had raised, phrasing the question as a reproachful reminder.
[JISHUMI:v7p5344/r16] JISHUMI, d. 494 · قيل | reports | One view is that Pharaoh mentioned raising Moses to display his favor to him.
[JISHUMI:v7p5344/r17] JISHUMI, d. 494 · قيل | reports | Another view is that Pharaoh invoked Moses' upbringing to deny his prophethood.
[JISHUMI:v7p5344/r18] JISHUMI, d. 494 · قيل | reports | A further possibility is that Pharaoh asked to establish whether Moses really was the same person.
[JISHUMI:v7p5344/r19] JISHUMI, d. 494 · قيل | reports | Moses reportedly lived among Pharaoh's people for thirty years.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p109/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Pharaoh says he raised Moses as a child in his household, where Moses lived for thirty years.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p227/r12] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Pharaoh’s question about raising Moses as a child is reproachful and belittling: he says he raised him and spared him among those he killed, then asks when Moses acquired his claimed mission.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p227/r13] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | Most readers pronounce ʿumruk with ḍamma on mīm; Abū ʿAmr reads ʿamruk with a still mīm.
[TABRISI:26:18-19/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | “Did we not raise you?” describes nurturing something through successive stages, meaning Pharaoh raised Moses from infancy.
[TABRISI:26:18-19/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says Moses lived with Pharaoh's people for eighteen years.
[TABRISI:26:18-19/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · مقاتل | reports | Mujahid says Moses lived with Pharaoh's people for thirty years.
[TABRISI:26:18-19/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · الكلبي | reports | Al-Kalbi says Moses lived with Pharaoh's people for forty years.
[TABRISI:26:18-19/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Pharaoh mentions raising Moses to claim credit for kindness toward him.
[TABRISI:26:18-19/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | Alternatively, Pharaoh reveals his meanness by recounting his favors.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses lived among them for eighteen years.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#2/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن السائب | reports | Ibn al-Sāʾib says Moses lived among them for forty years.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#2/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · مقاتل | reports | Muqātil says Moses lived among them for thirty years.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#2/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Pharaoh accuses Moses of repaying the favor of being raised by rejecting their kindness and killing one of their people.
[QURTUBI-FULL:26:16-19/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Pharaoh invokes Moses’ childhood upbringing to boast and belittle him: he raised him as a child and spared him when others were killed.
[QURTUBI-FULL:26:16-19/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | By asking how Moses spent years among them, Pharaoh challenges when Moses acquired the authority he now claims.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:26:16-18/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Pharaoh addressed Moses after the two came and delivered their message; in our midst means in our houses.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:26:16-18/r6] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | A walid is a child, named for being near birth.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:26:16-18/r7] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | An unnamed report says Moses stayed among them thirty years, spent ten in Midian, returned to call them to God for thirty years, and remained fifty after the drowning.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p181#5/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The words they went to Pharaoh and said are omitted for concision; walid means a child close to birth, so Pharaoh asks whether Moses was not young when they raised him.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p181#5/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · قيل | reports | One report says Moses lived among them for thirty years.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p145/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | An anonymous report says Pharaoh withheld access to Moses and Aaron for a year, then admitted them to laugh at the claimant; he recognized Moses and recalled raising him.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p145/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The narrative leaves implicit “they came to Pharaoh and said that to him,” which the context supplies.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p145/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Pharaoh dismisses the sender and message, belittles Moses, and invokes his childhood upbringing as a favor.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p145/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Pharaoh contrasts raising Moses to adulthood with killing Israelite boys of the same age, then recalls the killing of the Copt.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p145/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | وليد means a young child; it is on the فعيل pattern with passive meaning because the child is close to birth.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p145/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو عمرو | reports | In one transmission, Abū ʿAmr reads عمرك with a sukūn on its mīm; the dispute over the number of years was discussed in Ṭā Hā. | mentions 20:40
[SAMIN-DURR:26:18/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Walīdan is a circumstantial accusative of the object of nurabbika; it is on the faʿīl pattern with passive sense, naming the boy for what he once was.
[SAMIN-DURR:26:18/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Min ʿumrika is a circumstantial phrase modifying sinīna.
